correctness.rationale: For every edge, the degree sum is at most \(n+\operatorname{bk}(G)\). On a spectral-radius component, the standard edge degree-product bound and AM--GM give \(\lambda\le\frac12\max_{uv}(d(u)+d(v))\), hence the universal inequality. Equality forces equality throughout: the component is regular (the semiregular bipartite alternative also balances), spans all vertices, and every edge is dominating. Thus the complement has no induced three-vertex path and is a disjoint union of cliques; regularity forces those clique sizes to be equal. Equivalently, \(G\) is balanced complete multipartite. Direct substitution verifies the converse.
